S11.rationale: Deliberate, verifiable dismantling of capacity to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic and military incentives. No historical precedent for global irreversible renunciation of a general-purpose technology.

S1.rationale: Requires both global human extinction and collapse of AI infrastructure within 4.3 years. No plausible trajectory reaches mutual annihilation on that timescale.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction plus survival of a value-aligned successor AI by 2030. Aligned extinction is strictly less likely than misaligned extinction in this window.

S3.rationale: Misaligned AI causing human extinction by 2030 is the most plausible extinction path, but still requires rapid capability jump and deployment failure. Physical and institutional constraints keep the 4-year risk low.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of open-weight and state models could create a competitive multipolar AI ecology that marginalizes humans. By 2030 decisiveness is unlikely, but fragmentation is trending upward.

S5.rationale: Requires causally separated regions with different structural states by 2030. No space-based or otherwise causally isolated civilization will exist by then.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep brain-AI integration as the dominant structure requires breakthroughs and mass adoption not feasible by 2030. Augmentation will advance but remain tool-like.

S7.rationale: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive is plausible if AGI emerges 2027-2029 and centralizes quickly. Corporate and state incentives for autonomous deployment make this the main loss-of-control scenario by 2030.

S8.rationale: If transformative AI arrives by 2030, the first stable configuration is often a tense balance where neither humans nor AI can decisively dominate. This is the natural intermediate before lock-in or preserve.

S9.rationale: Base rate favors continuity: 4.3 years is short for civilization-wide power transfer and humans still control compute, energy, and deployment. This includes the sub-case where capabilities stay sub-transformative.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement system preventing structural change requires extraordinary coordination or unilateral control by 2030. Early prototypes of AI-enabled surveillance and governance make it non-negligible.

S11.rationale: Deliberate, verified global surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts economic and military incentives among major powers. No historical precedent for such coordinated renunciation exists.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Four-year simultaneous extinction of humanity and AI infrastructure has no historical base rate and requires planetary-scale collapse of biology and compute. Not credible by 2030 even with severe war or pandemic.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Requires human extinction plus a successfully value-aligned successor. The joint probability of both within four years is extremely low.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: The most cited extinction path is a misaligned superintelligence discarding humans. Still needs rapid, unchecked takeoff to completion by 2030.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: A multipolar swarm of competing AIs with no decisive coalition is plausible if open models proliferate quickly. Full human marginalization by 2030 remains unlikely, limiting probability.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Causally separated regions with different structural states requires self-sustaining off-Earth civilization, impossible by 2030 given launch and autonomy constraints.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration via uploading or radical augmentation remains lab-scale and not civilization-dominant by 2030 despite progress in BCI and bioengineering.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A superintelligent system could seize decisive power while keeping humans alive as dependents. Four years is short for full takeover, but fast takeoff scenarios make this the main alternative to continued human control.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Human institutions and AI systems remaining as peer powers captures a messy multipolar 2030 with strong AI but intact states and corporations. This is a natural intermediate before dominance or control.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Base rate is human control has held so far and transformative capability may not arrive or be deployed decisively by 2030; controls and inertia keep pace in most worlds.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Civilization-wide active prevention of structural change needs unprecedented global enforcement, at most narrow AI-enabled authoritarian entrenchment by 2030.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Requires deliberate, verifiable global dismantling of capability to build powerful AI. Coordination incentives point strongly against this within four years.
